brief: UBS derivatives desk argues the systematic-selling washout is complete: the last remaining seller, Risk Control, was overwhelmed by buying today instead of producing the expected Monday low. Risk Control exposure is 55% (1st percentile vs 1Y), the lowest since the tariff shock; the only two comparable washouts, 55% on Aug 6 2024 and 30% on Apr 10 2025, were followed by SPX gains of +17% and +24% over the next four months. CTA global equity exposure is negative at -5%, historically a bottoming signal when real-money investors are not selling, as is the case now. The desk concludes the downside feedback loop is largely removed: discretionary investors can still sell on headlines, but systematic funds are unlikely to amplify declines, and retail, foreign ETF buyers and returning buybacks should keep news-driven selloffs shallow. Intraday, S&P 500 and Nasdaq both show heavy buying ($34bn and $60bn), leveraged ETFs are buying $24bn, and CTAs have barely bought yet hold buy triggers higher in ES1 and RTY1. The desk expects SPX to grind at least +10% higher over the next three months.
